findings.reason: §6 must shrink to its two genuinely open items (extending `get_python_status`/`check_all_tools` to run under the block and report the floor, and retiring `data_access_patterns.setup_commands`) rather than re-propose a block and resolver the branch already carries, or the first §6 node will rebuild landed code.
findings.text: §6 describes "two homes" for the remote recipe and proposes giving it "one home, a facility-level `remote_environment` block" with "one resolver", but that exact machinery is already on this branch: `resolve_remote_environment` and the `RemoteEnvironment`/`RequiredModule` dataclasses are in `imas_codex/remote/environment.py` (commit 8f50f6642, an ancestor of HEAD 67af8f835), the schema block is at `imas_codex/schemas/facility_config.yaml:313` with `min_python_version` (378) and `required_modules` (383), the block is populated in `imas_codex/config/facilities/jt-60sa.yaml:25`, `iter.yaml:49` and `tcv.yaml:23`, and it is already consumed by `imas_codex/remote/tools.py:193` (`run_script`) and `imas_codex/discovery/signals/parallel.py:75` (`_facility_scanner_config`), whose docstring states the block-override precedence verbatim

findings.reason: naming `tools.py` as the resolver home invites a second merge path beside `remote/environment.py`, which is the placement duplication the rubric names; the plan should extend `remote/environment.py` and keep `tools.py` as a consumer.
findings.text: the plan says "One resolver in the facility-aware layer (`imas_codex/remote/tools.py`, which already resolves `ssh_host` and the nice level from facility config) merges the block", but `remote/tools.py` does not own resolution and must not: it imports `resolve_remote_environment` from `imas_codex/remote/environment.py:59` and passes the result down as executor parameters, and the signals pipeline reaches the same resolver through `parallel.py:75`

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §2 and §4 put new behaviour behind existing single entry points (the scanner config, the document pipeline), and §3 reuses the existing `WikiChunk-[:DOCUMENTS]->FacilitySignal` edge (written at `imas_codex/discovery/wiki/pipeline.py:319`, read at `imas_codex/llm/search_tools.py:547` and `:818`) rather than a second edge.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan names `imas_codex/remote/tools.py` as the resolver's home, but the resolver already lives in `imas_codex/remote/environment.py` and `tools.py` only consumes it, so placing new resolution logic in `tools.py` would fork the owner.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §3 names its one addition (`fronts_database`) and states in-text that it retires nothing and why, §6 names `data_access_patterns.setup_commands` as the thing it retires and states no CLI command is added, and §2's three FacilitySignal slots are accounted for in its locked decision (they replace the keywords stopgap).
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §6 proposes a facility-level `remote_environment` block and a resolver as if new, but both already exist on this branch (`imas_codex/remote/environment.py::resolve_remote_environment`, consumed by `imas_codex/remote/tools.py` and `imas_codex/discovery/signals/parallel.py`), so the section's central search is against a state the code has already moved past.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §3 and §6 each extend an existing owner (the wiki scorer and the remote-environment resolver/probe) with a stated reason, and §6 explicitly adds no new CLI command.
